content:
Apple Music Android version is getting a major redesign inspired by Liquid Glass in the latest 7.0 beta.

Following a year of Liquid Glass on Apple platforms, this new design language has officially arrived on Android. Apple Music now uses a floating bottom bar that allows content to be seen above, below, and on both sides. The navigation elements have a slight translucent effect, allowing the solid colour background beneath to be roughly visible.

New vs old

Similarly, the mini player at the top uses the same treatment and no longer attaches to the bottom bar. Compared with Liquid Glass on iOS, the bottom bar does not shrink into a smaller version when scrolling—everything stays in place.

The top bars throughout the app have been updated, with page titles and overflow menus now on the same line. The three-dot icon is no longer themed red and is now housed inside a circular container. The "Library" tab has seen the most extensive updates, with "Edit Pins" and "Edit Genres" now tucked inside the overflow menu.

The artist page has received a major overhaul: the background now adjusts its theme colour based on album artwork, closely matching the iOS design, the play button is more prominent, and the information page is no longer placed at the bottom. The share button has moved to the top-right corner.

The settings page has also been modernised with clearer groupings. The "Now Playing" section remains largely unchanged, and the iOS side has not seen any major updates either.

Finally, Apple Music 7.0 now uses an edge-to-edge design, with the status bar and navigation bar extending to the edges of the screen.

In its previous update, Apple Music for Android adopted a new version numbering system to align with iOS. This 7.0 version corresponds to iOS 27.

Apple Music 7.0 is still in beta, with the testing period typically lasting several weeks. You can sign up via the Play Store page or through this link. Overall, these beta versions have been fairly stable.
